topics.title: Getting started
topics.summary: Build and sell your first Signal Relay. The Guide button follows your progress in a new game.

sections.heading: 1. Mine iron
sections.text: Press 1 and click an Iron Ore outcrop on your HQ asteroid. Place a Refinery (2), choose Iron Bar as its recipe, then press N and click the Extractor followed by the Refinery to lay an Auto belt. Wait for an Iron Bar.

sections.heading: 2. Mine copper
sections.text: Place an Extractor (1) on Copper Ore and a second Refinery (2) set to Copper Bar. Press N and connect that Extractor to its Refinery. Keep both lines on your HQ asteroid.

sections.heading: 3. Assemble and sell
sections.text: Place an Assembler (3) and choose Signal Relay. It needs one Iron Bar and one Copper Bar. Use Auto belt (N) to connect each Refinery to the Assembler. Place a Sale Depot (4) and connect the Assembler to it. The Depot sells delivered Relays for credits; allow Signal Relays in its Settings if you changed its sell list.

sections.heading: 4. Grow from there
sections.text: Your HQ solar panels can power this first chain. Once it sells, tap an Ion Crystal with an Extractor to fund research. Select your HQ and press Research for new recipes, buildings and bonuses.

sections.heading: 5. Expand and win
sections.text: Claim cells with a unit, then deploy a Fort there from a Fort Construction Zone fed with Iron Plates and Copper Wire. Better craft need rare goods from those cells. Win by capturing the AI headquarters, or by trade: hold a high rate of sales of goods you make (see Credits and sales).

sections.heading: Bottleneck markers
sections.text: A machine that has spent much of the last half-minute stopped gets a marker: a pulsing red warning when an ingredient is missing with none on the way (starved), blue stacked crates when its output has nowhere to go (backed up), and a yellow bolt when power is short. Switch them off in Settings.

sections.heading: Speed and pause
sections.text: The top bar has Pause and 1x / 2x / 4x. Space pauses and resumes outside battles. While paused you can still look around, build, lay belts and give orders; nothing moves until you resume.

sections.heading: Production overview
sections.text: Production in the top bar (or P) lists, per good, how much you made, used and sold in the last minute of game time, and what was left over: green when you make more than you use, red when stock is being drawn down. Above it are your sales per minute and how close you are to the trade win. It fills up over a minute after a start or a load.

topics.title: Ion power
topics.summary: The stockpile that pays for research.

sections.heading: Where it comes from
sections.text: An Extractor on an Ion Crystal asteroid adds Ion to your stockpile every cycle, about 4 a second from a typical crystal. Ion is never carried on belts. It builds up slowly: plan research and ship orders around it.

sections.heading: What spends it
sections.text: Research and ships. Each research level costs credits and Ion (higher levels goods from Storage too), and ordering a ship costs Ion with its credits: Mobile Guard 20, Heavy Bomber 60, Rail Lancer 120, Flying Fortress 150. Machines and buildings never use Ion.

sections.heading: Getting more
sections.text: Tap more Ion asteroids and research Ion Resonance to raise their yield. Ion Efficiency makes research cost less Ion.

topics.title: Power
topics.summary: Solar capacity that keeps your machines running.

sections.heading: Supply
sections.text: Your Headquarters has solar panels built in (20 MW). Each Solar Array adds 6 MW. Photovoltaics research raises all solar by 25%.

sections.heading: Demand
sections.text: Machines draw power only while working: Extractor 1 MW, Refinery and Water Purifier 2, Assembler 3, Shipyard 4. Depots, Storage, Forts and belts draw nothing.

sections.heading: Overloaded
sections.text: The top bar shows demand / supply and, in brackets, your spare power. When it goes negative, every machine slows to supply ÷ demand. Nothing stops outright.

sections.heading: More power
sections.text: Build Solar Arrays in free slots: 3 in your HQ cell, 2 in each Fort cell. More slots means holding more cells.

topics.title: Belts
topics.summary: One-way conveyors that carry goods between buildings.

sections.heading: Drawing
sections.text: Press B, then left-drag from a building across neighbouring tiles. Each step lays one one-way belt for a small credit cost. Drawing over your own belt the other way reverses it for free.

sections.heading: Splits and merges
sections.text: Start a drag on an existing belt to branch off it, or finish on one to merge into it. Mixed goods can share a belt; each belt step carries one item at a time.

sections.heading: Auto belt
sections.text: Press N (or Auto belt in the build menu), click the machine the goods come from, then the machine they go to. The shortest free path lights up green as you point (red when it is blocked or you cannot afford it), and a click lays it at your chosen belt speed. It joins your existing belts where they already run the right way.

sections.heading: Lanes and speed
sections.text: Each belt carries one item at a time, at its own speed. A busy asteroid can fill one belt: run a second belt out of the extractor to the same machine or Storage and items split between the lanes. Keeping each good on its own lane beats one long mixed belt.

sections.heading: Drone links between asteroids
sections.text: Each cell is its own asteroid, with open space between them, and belts stop at the edge. To move goods to another asteroid, research Drone Logistics and build Drone Pads: link a pad to a tile on another asteroid within range and cargo drones carry goods across, one trip at a time. A link works both ways: machines on either asteroid can ask for goods made on the other, whichever pad you linked from. Shipping between asteroids is slow on purpose, so refine and assemble where the ore is and send finished goods. Select a link to see its flight time.

sections.heading: Upgrading
sections.text: Click a belt to select it; its whole line (up to the next building or junction) lights up. Upgrade that belt or the whole line to Fast Conveyor (cyan), then Express Conveyor (gold). You pay per belt, and belts already at that speed are free.

sections.heading: Who gets what
sections.text: Machines pull the ingredients they need through any connected route. Machines and shipyards are always served before Storage and Sale Depots, so depots only sell surplus.

sections.heading: Delivery priority
sections.text: Machines, Storage, Sale Depots, Shipyards and Fort zones have a delivery priority: Very low, Low, Normal, High or Very high. It only decides between buildings that want the same goods at the same moment: off a T-junction, a High tank fills before a Low shop, and the shop sells the overflow. It never carries on: whatever the tank passes on to machines behind it is shared by their own priorities. A machine's first batch is always served first, so priority can never stall a factory. Wiring the tank straight into the shop lets the shop draw from it. Set it with the row of buttons in the building's panel on the right.

sections.heading: Removing
sections.text: Press X and drag across belts to dismantle them. Items on a removed belt are lost.

sections.heading: Undo
sections.text: Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z on a Mac), or the Undo button in the top bar, takes back your last building or your last whole belt drag or auto belt for a full refund, as long as you placed it in the last minute. After that, Dismantle refunds half.

sections.heading: Belt View
sections.text: Press Belt View in the top bar (or V) when buildings hide your belts. Buildings fade and ignore clicks, so any click selects the belt there, and Dismantle only removes belts. Picking a building tool switches it off.

topics.title: Resource asteroids
topics.summary: Renewable deposits that Extractors mine.

sections.heading: Common
sections.text: Iron Ore, Copper Ore, Ice and Ion Crystal are found in every cell.

sections.heading: Rare
sections.text: Titanium Ore, Silicon Ore and Sulphur (gold glint) mine more slowly. Each HQ cell has one Silicon Ore asteroid; the rest sit in contested neutral cells.

sections.heading: Extra rare
sections.text: Unobtanium Ore, Complex Carbon and Gold Ore (gold halo) appear in a single cell each. Expect to fight for them.

sections.heading: Rich asteroids
sections.text: A gold ring marks a rich asteroid that mines faster than others of its kind. Asteroids never run out.

topics.title: Recipe tiers
topics.summary: Raw goods become bars, bars become components, components become assemblies.

sections.heading: Tier 1: refining
sections.text: Refineries turn each raw resource into a refined good: ore into bars, Ice into Water, Silicon Ore into Silicon Ingots, and so on.

sections.heading: Tier 2: components
sections.text: Assemblers turn refined goods into components such as Iron Plates, Copper Wire, Silicon Wafers and Titanium Struts. Water Purifiers make Purified Water.

sections.heading: Tier 3: assemblies
sections.text: Assemblers combine tier 1 and tier 2 goods into high-value assemblies like Electronics, Explosives and Reinforced Plate.

sections.heading: Unlocking
sections.text: Most components and assemblies must be researched first. A machine's recipe list shows how many recipes are still to discover.

topics.title: Extractor
topics.summary: Mines the asteroid it sits on.

sections.heading: Placing
sections.text: Press 1 and click an asteroid in a cell you own. One extractor per asteroid.

sections.heading: Output
sections.text: It mines three items per cycle into a small buffer, which connected machines pull from by belt. When the buffer cannot fit the next three it pauses until something takes its output.

sections.heading: Ion asteroids
sections.text: On an Ion Crystal, the extractor sends Ion straight to your stockpile instead; no belt needed.

topics.title: Refinery
topics.summary: Tier 1: turns a raw resource into a refined good.

sections.heading: Choosing a recipe
sections.text: A new refinery starts with no recipe and opens its Settings pop-up: pick one (for example Iron Bar from Iron Ore). Reopen Settings any time with the button in the side bar or C. It runs one recipe at a time; changing it resets progress. Copy settings and paste them onto other refineries (Ctrl/Cmd+C, Ctrl/Cmd+V).

sections.heading: What it needs
sections.text: A belt from an extractor (or storage) carrying the raw resource, power, and a belt out to whatever uses the result.

sections.heading: Reading it
sections.text: The Needs list shows each ingredient: green in stock, amber on the way, red missing. Floating icons over the machine show the same at a glance. In Settings, Machine needs shows them Always, On hover (only over the building under your mouse) or Never, and Belt item icons shows or hides the icon over each load on a belt.

sections.heading: Filling up
sections.text: Machines order enough ingredients to fill their storage. Each machine's first batch comes first, so on a shared line every machine gets started before any one fills up.

topics.title: Assembler
topics.summary: Tier 2 and 3: combines goods into components and assemblies.

sections.heading: Choosing a recipe
sections.text: A new assembler starts with no recipe and opens its Settings pop-up: pick one there (or later with Settings / C). Recipes still locked behind research show which research unlocks them; others are still undiscovered.

sections.heading: What it needs
sections.text: Belts bringing every ingredient of the chosen recipe (two inputs can share one merged belt), power, and a belt out to a buyer, another machine, storage or a shipyard.

sections.heading: Tips
sections.text: Wire and Wafer recipes make two items per cycle. If an assembler sits at 100%, it is waiting for room to put its output.

sections.heading: Filling up
sections.text: Machines order enough ingredients to fill their storage. Each machine's first batch comes first, so on a shared line every machine gets started before any one fills up.

topics.title: Water Purifier
topics.summary: Turns Water into Purified Water.

sections.heading: Unlocking
sections.text: Research Water Purification at your HQ.

sections.heading: Chain
sections.text: Ice asteroid, Extractor, Refinery set to Water, then a belt into the purifier. Purified Water sells well and goes into Coolant Cells.

topics.title: Sale Depot
topics.summary: Sells delivered goods for credits.

sections.heading: Selling
sections.text: Anything delivered is sold immediately at its price. Raw ore and Ion are not bought: refine them first. What you sell counts toward the trade win.

sections.heading: Sell list
sections.text: Select a depot to switch individual goods on or off, so it does not pull goods you would rather keep.

sections.heading: Priority
sections.text: Depots are served after machines and shipyards, so they only take surplus.

topics.title: Storage
topics.summary: A hub that collects surplus and supplies any connected machine.

sections.heading: Use
sections.text: Run several producer lines into one storage, then belts out to the machines that need the goods. It holds up to 200 items.

sections.heading: What it stores
sections.text: A new storage collects nothing until you choose: select it and press Settings to switch goods on, or use Store all and Store none to switch every good at once. Storages never feed each other.

topics.title: Shipyard
topics.summary: Builds craft from factory goods.

sections.heading: Ordering
sections.text: Select your shipyard, press Build (C) and pick a craft. The order costs credits up front; craft whose parts you have not researched are marked and cannot be ordered yet.

sections.heading: Parts
sections.text: The shipyard pulls the craft's parts along belts, then launches it once every part has arrived and the build time has passed.

sections.heading: What each craft needs
sections.text: Mobile Guard (100 credits, 20 Ion): 24 Iron Plate + 12 Copper Wire + 6 Relay. Heavy Bomber (350, 60 Ion): 12 Reinforced Plate + 12 Explosives + 6 Electronics, so Sulphur and Complex Carbon. Flying Fortress (850, 150 Ion): 12 Hull Section + 9 Field Emitter + 9 Coolant Cell + 12 Reinforced Plate + 6 Quantum Core, so Titanium, Unobtanium and Quantum Cores research. The credits are paid when you order; the shipyard builds once every part has arrived by belt, from production or Storage. It holds 56 parts, and a belt may end on any of its tiles, so feed it from several sides. With no order, it repairs your most damaged craft parked in its cell, one HP at a time: a Mobile Guard takes 2 Iron Plate per HP, a Heavy Bomber 1 Reinforced Plate and 1 Explosives, a Flying Fortress 1 Coolant Cell and 2 Purified Water. Each HP takes 5 seconds for a Mobile Guard, 8 for a Heavy Bomber and 12 for a Flying Fortress. Lost ships rejoin the fleet as it heals.

sections.heading: Craft types
sections.text: Mobile Guard: cheap and quick, a fleet of ten small ships with light to fair return fire; for claiming new cells and emergency defence, stronger as a cell's defender. Heavy Bomber: four big ships that hit hardest, with fair armour but weak return fire; send it to attack, not to defend. Flying Fortress: one huge shield flagship with heavy armour, the strongest return fire and a fair attack; every other ship of yours in its cell gets +1 armour, so fly it with your fleet. Rail Lancer: three long railgun ships that fire 9 from two cells away, where nothing can fire back, then recharge for 4 turns (Capacitor Banks research cuts that to 3, then 2). It has no armour or return fire, and up close its shot drops to 4 and the target answers, so keep it behind your line. A fleet loses ships as it loses HP.

topics.title: Fort
topics.summary: Holds a cell and switches its factory on.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: Outside your HQ cell, you can only build in a cell with a working Fort, and that cell's machines stop if the Fort is lost. An owned cell without a Fort or a unit reverts to neutral after a minute.

sections.heading: Getting one
sections.text: Forts are deployed from a Fort Construction Zone on the border of a neighbouring cell you hold. They cannot be placed directly.

sections.heading: Bonus
sections.text: A Fort cell has 2 Solar Array slots.

topics.title: Headquarters
topics.summary: Your base, your research office, and the target the AI is after.

sections.heading: Research
sections.text: Select it and press Research to open the research web.

sections.heading: Holding
sections.text: It holds its cell by itself and cannot be dismantled. Lose it and you lose the game; capture the AI's to win.

topics.title: Research
topics.summary: Discover recipes, buildings and bonuses at your HQ.

sections.heading: Opening
sections.text: Select your Headquarters and press Research. The game pauses while the web is open. Branches run left to right in coloured lanes. Drag anywhere to move the web (nodes too), click a node to see it, scroll or use + and − to zoom, and press F or Fit to see everything. Arrow keys or WASD also move it, and Enter researches the selected node.

sections.heading: Discovery
sections.text: Nodes you own or can buy show their names. A '?' outline is one step further out: buy what leads to it to reveal it. Anything further is hidden.

sections.heading: Costs
sections.text: Each level costs credits and Ion; ships are the only other thing that spends Ion. Multi-level nodes stack their bonuses.

sections.heading: Research time and the queue
sections.text: Research takes time: 2 minutes for a node with no prerequisites, and a minute more for each step further down the web and for each further level of the same node. You pay when you queue a level; up to 5 levels can wait in the queue, worked on one at a time, and you may queue a node behind the prerequisites already queued for it. The top bar shows what is being researched. Cancelling a queued level refunds everything paid for it, and anything queued behind it that needed it is cancelled and refunded too. Research pauses during battles. The AI works the same way, one level at a time.

sections.heading: What you get
sections.text: New recipes and buildings, faster machines and extractors, cheaper Ion use, more Ion yield and better sale prices. The AI researches too.

topics.title: Territory
topics.summary: Claim cells for their asteroids, then hold them.

sections.heading: Claiming
sections.text: Select one of your craft and right-click a neutral cell. Arriving in a clear cell claims it after a short hold.

sections.heading: Holding
sections.text: Keep a unit there until a Fort is deployed from a construction zone next door. Unguarded cells revert to neutral after a minute; the grid pulses orange as a warning. Only cells with your HQ or a Fort can run machines.

sections.heading: Losing a cell
sections.text: If a cell is captured, its machines stop. Recapture it within three minutes to get them back; after that they are cleared.

topics.title: Craft and battles
topics.summary: Units that claim, defend and attack cells.

sections.heading: Moving
sections.text: Select a craft and right-click a cell. Hovering shows what the click will do: move, claim or attack.

sections.heading: Four stats
sections.text: Every craft fights on Attack, Return fire, Armour and HP. A hit does Attack minus the target's Armour (at least 1). If the target survives and you are within its reach, it hits back with Return fire minus your Armour. Most craft fight neighbouring cells only; a Rail Lancer also fires from two cells away, out of everyone's reach. Each craft flies as a fleet: a Mobile Guard is ten ships (one per HP), a Heavy Bomber four ships twice the size (one per 3 HP), a Flying Fortress one huge ship. Ships drop out as the craft loses HP.

sections.heading: Damage falls with HP
sections.text: A damaged craft's Attack and Return fire shrink with its remaining HP, so attacking first matters and wounded craft hit back softer.

sections.heading: Battles
sections.text: Attacking a defended cell starts a turn-based battle and pauses the factory. Every ship in the battle acts once a turn: attack, move or hold the control point. Ships nearby can join by moving into a battle cell, which uses their turn. Right-click an enemy ship or Fort to choose your target. Press Space to end your turn, or retreat. An attacker that has not won by the end of round 10 is fatigued and withdraws home.

sections.heading: Battle scenes
sections.text: Each attack plays a short scene: your formation and theirs, one ship per fifth of HP. Click to skip. Choose Off, Fast or Full under Battle scenes in the menu.

sections.heading: Defenders
sections.text: Each cell has one defender, which gets its defender bonus. A cell's Fort and its defender protect the other ships there: they must fall before anything else in the cell can be targeted. When the defender falls, a reserve takes over. A Fort has 10 HP and armour 3 and fires back (5) at attackers next to it, but never attacks; a Rail Lancer can shell it from two cells away. If a Fort is destroyed while no attacker stands in its cell, its owner has 2 minutes to deploy a new Fort there or the cell turns neutral.

sections.heading: Repairs
sections.text: Select a damaged unit and press Return for repairs to send it to your nearest reachable shipyard. A shipyard repairs a docked unit one HP at a time while it is not building a ship, using that unit's repair parts delivered by belt.

sections.heading: Groups
sections.text: Order several units at once. With a mouse, drag a box over them on the map, or Shift-click units to add or remove them (Shift with a box adds to what is selected). On a touch screen, switch on Group in the touch bar, then tap units. A selected unit's panel also offers Select all my units here. Right-click (or long-press) a cell and every unit in the group holds, attacks or travels there; if a battle starts at once, the units still on their way can join it as reinforcements. Return for repairs sends every damaged unit in the group to its nearest shipyard. Esc clears the selection.

sections.heading: AI battle turns
sections.text: Settings has AI battle turns: Watch plays the AI's moves one at a time, Quick plays them faster, and Instant resolves its whole turn at once, skipping its attack scenes and summing the damage up in the status bar.

sections.heading: Shield flagship
sections.text: A Flying Fortress shields the rest of its side's ships in its cell: each has +1 armour while it is there (it does not shield itself, and two Fortresses do not stack). Bring it with the fleet that attacks, or park it where your defender sits. Enemy Fortresses shield enemy ships the same way.

topics.title: Credits and sales
topics.summary: Money for building, and the sales total you need to win.

sections.heading: Earning
sections.text: Every item a Sale Depot sells adds its price to your credits and to your sales total. Depots do not buy raw ore or Ion: refine it at least once. Each step further up the chain is worth more for the power it uses, and Quantum Cores, Precision Circuits and Field Emitters pay best.

sections.heading: Spending
sections.text: Buildings, belts, craft orders and research cost credits. Spending never lowers your sales total. Dismantling refunds half a building's cost.

sections.heading: Trade win
sections.text: Sell goods you make at a set rate and hold it for 30 seconds: 6,000 credits a minute on Easy, 10,000 on Medium, 25,000 on Hard (chosen on the title screen for a new game). The rate is measured over the last 30 seconds, and each good counts only as far as you also made it in that time, so saving goods up and selling them all at once does not help: it takes factories that keep making and selling. The top bar shows your rate against the target, and the countdown once you reach it. Roughly: Easy needs 4 to 6 asteroids producing well, Medium about 8, Hard well-planned high-tier lines.

topics.title: Solar Array
topics.summary: Adds 6 MW of solar power.

sections.heading: Building it
sections.text: 80 credits plus 4 Copper Bars and 2 Silicon Ingots, taken from your Storage buildings when you place it. No belt needed.

sections.heading: Slots
sections.text: Each array needs a free slot: 3 in your HQ cell and 2 in each cell held by a Fort. Your HQ cell has a Silicon Ore asteroid, so you can make Silicon Ingots at home.

topics.title: Fort Construction Zone
topics.summary: Builds a Fort for the neighbouring cell, from goods your factory delivers.

sections.heading: Placing
sections.text: Put it on an edge tile of a cell you hold, facing the cell you want to expand into (not a corner). 150 credits.

sections.heading: Filling
sections.text: Belt in 6 Iron Plates and 4 Copper Wire from your local factory. The zone shows what it still needs.

sections.heading: Deploying
sections.text: Once it is full and you hold the neighbouring cell (claim it with a unit), the zone deploys a Fort there and disappears. That cell's factory comes online.

topics.title: Drone Pad
topics.summary: Sends goods to another of your asteroids by cargo drone.

sections.heading: Unlocking
sections.text: Research Drone Logistics (Logistics branch) to build Drone Pads. Belts stop at an asteroid's edge, so pads are the only way to move goods between asteroids.

sections.heading: Linking
sections.text: Select a pad: a ring shows its drone range. Press Link, then click a tile on another asteroid you hold inside the ring. A receiving pad is built there (or the link joins a pad already standing there). Each pad sends to one place; pick a new tile to relink, or Unlink. A pad can also pass goods on: link a receiving pad onward to reach further asteroids.

sections.heading: Belts
sections.text: Belt goods into the sending pad and belt them away from the receiving pad. Routes run through pads like junctions.

sections.heading: Drones
sections.text: The drone loads at the pad, flies across, drops its load and flies home before taking the next. Flight time grows with distance. Upgrade the link (select it) or research Drone Engines to fly faster, Cargo Drones to carry more per trip, and further Drone Logistics levels for more range.
